A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NashPG and contain readable main text and Appendices A–C. Their equations, tables, figures and corresponding passages support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original exploitability measurements, head-to-head results and ablations across seven games, plus the regularization-annealing experiment in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised main-result aggregates, including Figures 1–5 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The IMMD and NashPG procedures, Algorithms 3–4 and objectives in Equations 11–12 remain unchanged. The natural-gradient correction and added derivation concern the mathematical justification of the existing mirror step.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven games under the same task requirements: Kuhn Poker, Leduc Poker, abrupt Dark Hex, abrupt Phantom Tic-Tac-Toe, Liar’s Dice, Battleship and Heads-Up NLHE. Appendix C retains the Kuhn Poker annealing scenario.

E2.justification: NFSP, PSRO, MMD and R-NaD remain the benchmark comparators. The sensitivity comparisons retain MMD and R-NaD, and Figure 5 retains RNaD-PPO. The added discussion of CFR methods does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics and the 1,024-game head-to-head protocol remain unchanged. The 10,000-update best-response budget emphasized in v3 Section 5.1 was already specified in v2 Appendix B.4; the changed seed count belongs to uncertainty reporting.

E4.justification: The regularization-sensitivity study, NeuRD-to-PPO ablation and Appendix C annealing analysis retain their questions and tested configurations. Existing plots receive numerical updates, but no additional ablation, robustness scenario or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Main evaluations change from four to five reported seeds/runs in Section 5.1, Figures 3–4, Table 3 and Appendix B.4. Table 3 adds flags for means within one standard deviation of zero. Mean±standard-deviation reporting continues, while Appendix C still specifies four runs.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 and all twelve Table 3 payoff summaries are updated, with broadly retained trends. For example, NashPG versus MMD changes from +0.010±0.040 to +0.008±0.035 in Liar’s Dice and from +0.105±0.021 to +0.111±0.023 in Heads-Up Poker. These are revised aggregates using five rather than four runs; Figure 6 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 1 and 3 and Lemma 2 now explicitly require an equilibrium in int dom ψ ∩ Z. Appendix A.5.1 revises the convergence proof’s compactness and interior-limit argument. New Proposition 1 in Appendix A.5 derives natural-gradient first-order equivalence, correcting v2’s ordinary-gradient statement. These materially revise the central theoretical foundation.

C1.justification: The headline convergence result in the introduction is narrowed to require an interior-domain equilibrium, and Section 4.2 removes the claim that IMMD introduces no assumptions beyond MMD convergence. This materially restricts the central guarantee. The abstract also changes the head-to-head claim from higher payoff to comparable or higher payoff.

C2.justification: v3 explains the boundary-equilibrium limitation and the dependence of KL visitation weights on both players. It identifies approximate exploitability as a best-response-quality-dependent lower bound, qualifies the near-zero MMD comparisons, and restricts the inner-optimizer explanation to larger games. The conclusion adds a finite-time-bound hypothesis connecting regularization strength to performance.

D1.justification: The code-access target changes from easonyu0203/nash_policy_gradient_public to ntu-agents/nashpg. Section 5.1 newly specifies that best-response agents share the policy agents’ architecture. The remaining implementation settings and appendix hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Eckstein (1993) and Censor et al. (1998), explicitly identifying IMMD’s outer loop as a classical Bregman proximal-point method. It also uses the already-cited Rudolph et al. benchmark to justify excluding model-free CFR comparators. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized explanatory revisions, updated author information and author–year citations. v3 adds a Broader Impact Statement and Appendix A.5, moving the existing convergence proof from A.4.4 to A.5.1.

P2.justification: The entire paper adopts the TMLR template, changing typography, title and author layout, headers, spacing and figure/table placement. Figures 1–5 are replotted and resized, Figure 4 gains an explicit Approximate Exploitability label, and Table 3 adds dagger annotations and an explanatory caption. The existing figure and table inventory is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through explicit equilibrium conditions, the natural-gradient derivation, and better qualifications of approximate exploitability and near-zero head-to-head margins. These are useful but limited gains: the abstract and conclusion retain broad convergence wording, and the general five-seed statement conflicts with Appendix C’s retained four runs.
